bugs.error_message: User-reported: 'I can not assign a member of Grazer VSC to a newly created team. The members are not listed.'
bugs.root_cause: TeamMembership.user required a registered User (not the ClubMember roster), and AddMemberView's picker only ever queried [User]. Most Grazer VSC roster entries (ClubMember) have no matching app account, since they're admin-entered roster data, not sign-ups — so they never appeared as assignable team members. Not a code defect so much as a design gap: two separate 'member' concepts (registered User vs. roster ClubMember) with no bridge between them for team assignment.
bugs.fix: Made TeamMembership.user optional and added an optional TeamMembership.clubMember, exactly one set per membership. Added TeamMembership.displayName/.subtitle computed helpers so rendering code doesn't need to know which side is set. AddMemberView now shows two Picker sections: 'Registrierte Benutzer' and 'Grazer VSC Mitglieder ohne Konto'. CloudKitSync publishes/resolves either userID or clubMemberID on the TeamMembership record. EventParticipation was deliberately left untouched (self-registering for an event still requires an account).

bugs.error_message: User-reported: 'the export of members of a training is not possible. The app crashes.'
bugs.root_cause: ActivityView (UIViewControllerRepresentable wrapping UIActivityViewController, used by MemberListView.exportTeilnehmerliste to share the generated .xlsx via a second .sheet) never configured popoverPresentationController.sourceView/sourceRect. UIActivityViewController defaults to popover presentation style on iPad (this app supports iPad via TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY '1,2' in project.yml) — with no popover anchor, UIKit throws an uncaught NSInvalidArgumentException at presentation time and the app hard-crashes. This is a UIKit-level fatal exception, not a thrown Swift Error, so MemberListView.exportTeilnehmerliste's existing do/catch (bug-066) could never have caught it — the export/zip-generation logic itself was already verified correct (see cerebrum 2026-07-17 TeilnehmerInnenliste entry).
bugs.fix: ActivityView.makeUIViewController now sets popover.sourceView (to the key window's root view) and popover.sourceRect (centered) whenever controller.popoverPresentationController is non-nil, with permittedArrowDirections = [] since there's no specific anchor button to point at. Verified: clean xcodebuild for iphonesimulator (BUILD SUCCEEDED, 0 errors), then installed + launched on an iPad Air (M4) simulator and confirmed the process stays alive (no immediate crash). Could not drive the full export flow end-to-end in-session since the app requires real Apple ID / CloudKit sign-in, not automatable from a coding sandbox.

bugs.error_message: User-reported (follow-up to bug-070): 'the app crashed again' on the export flow, clarified as a permanent freeze (not a crash) on iPhone von Franz with VoiceOver running
bugs.root_cause: MemberListView presented its own share sheet (ActivityView/UIActivityViewController) as a second .sheet nested directly on top of the first .sheet (MemberListView itself, presented from Training/TournamentDetailView). This sheet-on-a-sheet pattern froze the main thread only when VoiceOver was running (VoiceOvers synchronous accessibility-tree recompute does not tolerate a second modal presented while the first is still resolving) -- never reproduced with VoiceOver off, and the bug-070 iPad-popover fix was unrelated/insufficient since this device is an iPhone. No crash/hang report was ever generated on-device (confirmed via repeated xcrun devicectl device info files --domain-type systemCrashLogs polling and a manually-triggered sysdiagnose) because iOS does not watchdog-kill an app that is merely stuck in the foreground, only for lifecycle-transition timeouts.
bugs.fix: MemberListView no longer manages its own share-sheet state -- it now takes an onExported: (URL) -> Void closure and calls dismiss() + onExported(url) on successful export instead of presenting ActivityView itself. TrainingDetailView and TournamentDetailView each added exportedFileURL/showShareSheet state and now present the share sheet from .sheet(isPresented: showMemberList binding, onDismiss: { if exportedFileURL != nil { showShareSheet = true } }) -- i.e. only after the member-list sheet has fully finished dismissing, eliminating the nested-sheet presentation entirely. Could not verify the VoiceOver-specific freeze is gone end-to-end in-session (requires real device + VoiceOver + full login/team/training/attendance setup, not automatable from this sandbox) -- user should retest the export flow with VoiceOver on before considering this closed.

bugs.error_message: User asked for 'an easier possibility to update or insert data in the cloudkit data model' -- updates to existing CloudKit records were unreliable/silent-failing
bugs.root_cause: Every push* function builds a brand-new CKRecord(recordType:recordID:) instance rather than fetching the existing server record first, so it never carries a recordChangeTag. The shared save() helper called CKDatabase.save(_:), whose default save policy (.ifServerRecordUnchanged) treats a record with no change tag as an unverifiable conflict against any existing server record with the same recordID -- so CKError.serverRecordChanged is thrown on the second and every subsequent push of the same id (i.e. inserts worked, updates silently failed). The error was only printed to the console (print(...) inside a Task's catch), never surfaced, so it looked like intermittent/silent update failures rather than a clear crash.
bugs.fix: Replaced the single-record CKDatabase.save(_:) call in the private save(_:) helper (and the separate inline save in pushEventImage) with a CKModifyRecordsOperation configured with savePolicy = .changedKeys, wrapped in withCheckedThrowingContinuation for async/await use (new private upsert(_:) method). .changedKeys always writes the fields present on the record regardless of whether a server copy exists or what its change tag is, making every push* function a true insert-or-update with no conflict handling needed.

bugs.error_message: User-reported: 'When i open the one training in the Trainings view, the app crashed.' — real crash confirmed via devicectl crash log (EXC_BREAKPOINT/SIGTRAP, fatal SwiftData assertion) inside TeamMembership.id.getter, called from TrainingDetailView.attendance(for:)'s `training.attendances.first { $0.membership.id == membership.id }`.
bugs.root_cause: Attendance.membership: TeamMembership is a non-optional to-one relationship with no explicit @Relationship deleteRule/inverse declared on the TeamMembership side. TeamsViews' roster swipe-to-delete (and Team's own cascade delete of its memberships) called modelContext.delete(membership) directly. SwiftData's default deleteRule for an undeclared to-one relationship is .nullify, which cannot null a non-optional Swift property — this corrupts the dependent Attendance's local backing row instead of failing cleanly. Any later access to that Attendance's membership.id (TrainingDetailView/TournamentDetailView.attendance(for:)) then crashes with a fatal SwiftData assertion (_assertionFailure inside the @Model-macro-generated id getter). Compounding gap: neither the membership delete nor the team delete ever pushed a CloudKit delete (no deleteMembership/deleteTeam existed in CloudKitSync.swift), so a 'deleted' membership would also silently reappear on the next pull.
bugs.fix: Added an explicit @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \Attendance.membership) var attendances: [Attendance] = [] to TeamMembership (Models.swift), so deleting a TeamMembership now cascade-deletes its dependent Attendance records instead of corrupting them. Added CloudKitSync.deleteMembership(_:) and .deleteTeam(_:) (mirroring the existing deleteMember/deleteUserIdentity/deleteEventImage pattern) and wired them into TeamsListView.deleteTeams and TeamDetailView's roster .onDelete, plus added the missing modelContext.save() calls at both sites. bugs.error_message: User-reported: 'all data were deleted. and where is the Benutzerverwaltung?' — after this agent uninstalled+reinstalled the app on the physical device to fix bug-163's corrupted local store.
bugs.root_cause: RootView.resolveAccount()'s account-matching relies on two things that a full app UNINSTALL wipes simultaneously: the local SwiftData store (so the local `users.first(where: appleUserIdentifier ==)` lookup finds nothing) AND the @AppStorage-backed storedAppleUserIdentifier/storedUserID (UserDefaults is also cleared on uninstall, so the compensating id-based re-link path is gone too). Apple Sign-In only sends a real email/fullName on the very first-ever grant for an Apple ID + bundle/team combo, never again — not even after reinstall — so the post-reinstall sign-in returned a userIdentifier with nil email/fullName. With no local match and no identifying info from Apple, resolveAccount()'s final fallback branch silently created a brand-new blank 'Neues Mitglied' User (role: member, isRoot: false) instead of recognizing this was a returning user. The real account's data was never actually deleted — CloudKit still has it — but the user was now logged into a disconnected, empty, non-admin account, which explained both symptoms: apparently-empty Teams/Trainings/Tournaments lists (filtered by the new blank account's empty memberships) and the missing 'Benutzerverwaltung'/'Benutzer verwalten' buttons (gated on role==admin||isRoot, which the new account has neither).
bugs.fix: Added a check in resolveAccount(): when Apple Sign-In returns both nil fullName and empty/nil email (the documented signature of a repeat, non-first grant) and no local account matched, the code now awaits CloudKitSync.shared.syncAll() to pull down existing accounts and then returns without creating a new user, falling through to LoginView's account picker instead of guessing. This lets the user pick their real (now locally re-synced) account, or the accidentally-created blank duplicate can be deleted via the existing swipe-to-delete on LoginView/UserListView. Recovery for the user's current device: log out (Account tab -> Abmelden) and pick the real account from the list — CloudKitSync's background sync (triggered even on the blank-account creation path) should already have pulled the real UserIdentity record back down locally.

Root cause of the original failure was never conclusively isolated to app code; most likely a stale/suspended prior app instance on the device, resolved by the forced relaunch. Separately (unrelated to the import, caught live on the console during this session): the on-device CloudKit container is missing production schema setup -- several record types (SportEvent, Tournament, EventImage, EventParticipation, TournamentAttendance) do not exist server-side at all, and several existing types (UserIdentity, ClubMember, Team, TeamMembership, Training, TrainingAttendance) have their recordName field not marked Queryable, both of which make CloudKitSync.pull* silently fail (errors only reach the console, never surfaced in-app) for those record types.

The CloudKit schema gaps (missing record types + non-queryable recordName index) were NOT fixed in this session -- need the CloudKit Dashboard schema for the Production environment reviewed/deployed (Development schema likely has these record types/indexes already from local testing, Production does not), otherwise cross-device sync of Sport events/Tournaments/EventImages/Participations/Attendance silently fails for every user.

bugs.error_message: Default teams (Grazer VSC Damen/Herren, Blindenfussball, Helfer) were not created automatically on device after deploy
bugs.root_cause: ensureDefaultTeams only ran once, right after the first syncAll at cold launch, and bailed out silently (by design, to avoid duplicate-team races) if the CloudKit existence query failed even once. Cold launch is exactly when a CKQuery is most likely to transiently fail while the container/account is still becoming ready, so a single failure meant the feature never fired again for that whole app session.
bugs.fix: Added a 3-attempt retry (2s apart) inside ensureDefaultTeams before giving up, and added .refreshable to TeamsListView (mirroring MembersListView) so pull-to-refresh re-runs syncAll + ensureDefaultTeams as a manual fallback.

bugs.error_message: Default teams (and likely other CloudKit-synced data) still not appearing automatically even after adding retry + pull-to-refresh
bugs.root_cause: triggerBackgroundSync() (syncAll + ensureDefaultTeams) was only ever called from the 3 Apple-Sign-In-driven branches inside resolveAccount(). The plain LoginView(onLogin:) closure -- used whenever an account is picked from the login list, or after RegisterView.onRegister -- set currentUser directly and never called it. Any user whose session lands on that path (e.g. no working Apple ID sign-in state on this device) never synced at all, regardless of retries, since the sync call itself never happened.
bugs.fix: Added triggerBackgroundSync() to the onLogin closure in RootView.body, so every path that lands on a currentUser (Apple-driven or manual picker/register) now triggers the same background sync + default-team ensure.

bugs.error_message: Default teams still not appearing at all (not even locally) after fixing both the retry gap (bug-184) and the missing sync trigger on the manual login path (bug-185)
bugs.root_cause: ensureDefaultTeams gated ALL local team creation behind a live CKQuery existence check (guard let existingNames = await existingTeamNames() else return), on the theory that this avoids a cross-device duplicate-team race. But local SwiftData team creation does not actually need CloudKit at all -- only pushTeam does. If CloudKit was unreachable/unauthenticated on this device for any reason, that guard silently blocked EVERYTHING, including the purely-local insert, no matter how many times ensureDefaultTeams was retried or from which call site it was triggered. This is why bug-184s retry fix and bug-185s missing-trigger fix both failed to resolve the symptom -- neither addressed the real blocker.
bugs.fix: Removed the live CKQuery gate entirely. ensureDefaultTeams now checks the LOCAL store for existing team names (syncAll already ran immediately before every call site, so local state already reflects the latest known remote data) and always creates+inserts any missing default teams locally, regardless of CloudKit reachability. pushTeam is still called per new team for eventual cross-device sync, but its success is no longer a precondition for local visibility. Confirmed working live on-device by the user 2026-08-03.

iOS Device Deploy workflow failed: "Provisioning profile 'iOS Team Provisioning Profile: it.a11y.BlindensportGraz' doesn't include the Push Notifications capability" / "doesn't include the aps-environment entitlement"
bugs.root_cause: The app's entitlements file gained aps-environment (Push Notifications) in an earlier commit (8d3e500, "Push notifications for team members when a Training/Tournament is created"), which requires the App ID's Push Notifications capability to be enabled in the Apple Developer portal and a matching provisioning profile. The CI workflow's provisioning profile is a static, pre-harvested .mobileprovision stored as the IOS_CI_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 GitHub secret (see the 2026-07-17 self-hosted-runner cerebrum entry) -- it predates the push-notification feature and was never regenerated/re-uploaded, so it lacks the aps-environment entitlement xcodebuild now requires to match BlindensportGraz.entitlements.
bugs.fix: Final root cause and fix, after 5 CI attempts: (1) Portal capability + fresh profile — user-side, correct. (2) stale-profile cleanup in 'Install provisioning profile' — correct, verified only one profile remains. (3) attempted CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual + PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER scoped via a '$SCHEME:SETTING=value' xcodebuild CLI prefix — this syntax does NOT exist; xcodebuild just echoes it back as an unrecognized literal key without applying it, so CODE_SIGN_STYLE silently stayed at project.yml's Automatic default and reproduced the exact original error (confirmed by the byte-identical placeholder profile name 'iOS Team Provisioning Profile: it.a11y.BlindensportGraz' in the error, which doesn't even match the real installed profile's Name field 'BlindensportGraz CI Development'). (4) a plain global CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual + PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER override DOES apply, but also lands on the ZIPFoundation SPM dependency's resource-bundle target ('ZIPFoundation_ZIPFoundation does not support provisioning profiles ... Set the provisioning profile value to Automatic') since xcodebuild command-line overrides are never actually target-scoped — there is no real per-target CLI syntax. FIX: added a new 'Configure Manual signing on the app target' step that installs the `xcodeproj` Ruby gem and directly edits the generated .xcodeproj's BlindensportGraz-target-only Debug build configuration (CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual, PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER=$PROFILE_UUID) — genuinely per-target since it edits the actual pbxproj structure rather than relying on any CLI scoping mechanism; the SPM package is a structurally separate project XCBuild resolves independently, never touched by this edit. 'Build for device' no longer passes CODE_SIGN_STYLE/PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER on the command line at all (baked into the project already), keeping only CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY/DEVELOPMENT_TEAM/OTHER_CODE_SIGN_FLAGS as before. Verified end-to-end on this Mac (which IS the runner) before trusting it in CI: xcodegen generate -> ruby patch -> confirmed single, correctly-scoped pbxproj occurrence -> real `xcodebuild build` against the physical device destination got all the way past provisioning/capability validation with zero Push-Notifications or ZIPFoundation errors, only failing at the unrelated, already-documented errSecInternalComponent sandboxed-codesign limitation (bug-008) specific to this coding session's own shell — the real CI workflow's ephemeral, non-interactively-unlocked keychain doesn't hit that wall. Reverted the local test mutation to BlindensportGraz.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj before committing (it's tracked, not gitignored).

bugs.root_cause: MemberImportExport.importMembers(...) (MemberImportExport.swift:303) calls CloudKitSync.shared.pushMember(member) as a side effect of a plain import — CloudKitSync.shared lazily constructs a real CKContainer. Running xcodebuild test with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO (required in this sandboxed session because real codesigning hits a separate sandbox wall, see the 2026-07-15 Do-Not-Repeat entries) strips the app's iCloud entitlement, so the moment any code path touches CKContainer the process hard-crashes (not a catchable Swift error) — this is a CloudKit SDK behavior, not an app bug. Every other test suite in the target passed cleanly (72/72 across InheritanceQueryTests/KostZCalculationTests/PraeCalculationTests/TeilnehmerlisteExportTests/TrainingsfrequenzlisteCalculationTests) in the same run — only MemberImportExportTests exercises a CloudKitSync push path, which is why it's the only suite affected. This superseded an earlier same-session guess that this was generic simulator flakiness (see cerebrum.md's 2026-08-05 Do-Not-Repeat entry) — it is fully reproducible, not flaky, and unrelated to any change made this session.
bugs.fix: Not fixed — this only manifests when running unit tests unsigned (CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO), which this sandboxed session requires. No code change was made since MemberImportExportTests' behavior (pushing to CloudKit on import) is correct/intended for a real signed build; the crash is purely a side effect of stripping entitlements for local unsigned test runs. Workaround options for a future session, none applied: (1) run tests from a properly signed context (Xcode GUI, or a CI runner with real signing) where the entitlement is present; (2) inject a fake/no-op CloudKitSync for tests via dependency injection, which would be a real (larger) refactor, not attempted here since it wasn't asked for.
